newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. DEBT VOLS FIRM AS BONDS REMAIN WEAK.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. DEBT VOLS FIRM AS BONDS REMAIN WEAK.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were fimer in late trade as the underlying markets remained soft and nervousness persisted ahead of some key economic data due out later in the week, dealers said.
Although there was perception that the steep downturn in fixed income asset prices this month might have been overdone, the downward momentum had yet to abate, they said.
"People are pumping up volatility before this week's numbers," said a bank affiliate trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) Treasury bond pit.

Implied volatility for September T-bond futures options, which expire in less than two weeks and thus have relatively high gamma, rose to around 9.5 percent from Friday's 9.0 percent close. Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which provides quicker premium acceleration.
Volatility for Decembers, which are less sensitive to bond price movement, also rose a few tenths of a point to 8.6 percent.
Among the data due out this week, the most closely watched were Wednesday's July retail sales and producer price index (PPI) and Thursday's consumer price index (CPI).
A rise in energy prices might have buoyed the overall PPI and CPI in July, one trader said, adding that the market would be quick to react on any bearish news.

According to a Reuters poll, Wall Street economists have, on average, forecast retail sales to be up 0.7 percent in July against a 0.5 percent rise in June. Estimates for both overall and core PPI averaged at up 0.1 percent, while those for both overall and core CPI averaged at up 0.2 percent.
Among the largest trades in the CBOT bond pit, a brokerage firm was said to have bought 2,000 contracts of September 114 calls.

Traders said CBOT's 10-year T-note futures options saw some big orders. An investment bank traded 5,000 lots of September 108-109 combo, buying the 108 puts and selling the 109 calls. Another bank bought 3,000 of December 110 puts.
Implied volatility for December 10-year T-note futures options was a touch firmer at around 5.3 percent.
At the shorter end of the curve, activity in Eurodollar options was somewhat subdued, with a mixed bag of medium-sized trades going through both ways, traders said.
Volatilities for December and March Eurodollar futures options were marginally higher at about 9.0 and 11.2 percent.
